description:
Why Do Astronauts Age Slower Than You?

Episode 70 of a daily journey through the universe. ⏳
Time dilation: Einstein showed that time runs slower when you move fast or sit deeper in gravity. GPS satellites must correct their clocks by about 38 microseconds a day, and astronauts on the ISS age a tiny bit slower.

segments.text: If you went to space, you'd come back younger than everyone else. Really.
Time feels the same for everyone. One second is one second. But Einstein discovered that's not true.
segments.headline: Is time the same for all?

segments.text: The faster you move, the slower your time runs, compared to someone standing still.
segments.headline: Speed slows time

segments.text: And the closer you are to something massive, the slower time runs too. Gravity bends time.
segments.headline: Gravity slows time

segments.text: This isn't just theory. It happens to the GPS satellites guiding your phone right now.
segments.headline: In your pocket

segments.text: Their clocks run about thirty-eight microseconds a day faster than clocks on the ground.
If engineers didn't correct for it, GPS positions would drift by roughly ten kilometers every day.
Astronauts on the space station move so fast that they age a tiny bit slower. After six months, they're a few milliseconds younger.
segments.headline: Astronauts age slower

segments.text: Near a black hole, the effect would be enormous. An hour there could equal years far away.
segments.headline: Near a black hole

segments.text: Tomorrow, could there be shortcuts through space and time? Next stop: wormholes. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
